_comment: The judge's limits and calibration, stated once; every size, endpoint, key name and judge-specific threshold is read from here (judge_profile.py for Python, src/judge-profile.ts for Node, which apply the same rules). SUPERJEV_JUDGE picks the profile (default below; 'fake' is the test judge and uses the default's numbers). kind names the implementation that speaks to it. key_env is the environment variable holding its API key. aliases are other accepted names. window_tokens is the judge's hard input ceiling for the state plus the longest question; bytes_per_token is the one size rule (judge tokens = UTF-8 bytes / this, rounded up, high on purpose); input_cap_headroom is the room left under the window for the question battery, call_headroom how far one call's budget sits under the input cap; max_questions_per_call is how many questions one call may carry; input_usd_per_mtok is its published input price per million tokens; max_parts is how many judge calls one direct check may need before it is refused; file_ceiling_bytes is the largest file that connects whole; gate_window_tokens is the evidence window the Stop gate sends; overloaded_statuses are the HTTP codes that mean try again, retried retry_attempts times starting retry_first_delay_ms apart (doubling); too_big_status is the code that means the request was over the window. The calibration numbers are measured for one judge and must be re-measured for another: confidence_line (under it a human reads the source), sure_line, confirm_floor, source_floor, claim_content_floor, route_floor, preflight_strong (ask.py), outcome_line and max_confidence_above_peak (the organizer/outcome accept gate; Node reads both). NOT YET IN THIS TABLE (checklist for the next judge, re-measure each): fetch.ts:471,484; sweep.ts:66; superjev.py:515,1513,1527,4191,4193; ask.py SPREAD_CAP, NEAR_TWIN_GAP, FALLBACK_REL_FLOOR, SUBJECT_MATCH_FLOOR; and the batch sizes (40/45/20/5), chunking (12000/3500, coverage 0.75), sweep reask [0.70,0.90), overclaim 0.50/0.995, noul 0.6/0.4. OPTIONAL per profile: api_url_env (an environment variable that, when set, replaces api_url), key_required (false for a judge that takes no key: no key check, no Authorization header; default true), confidence_field (the reply field the confidence numbers read, default 'confidence'; the lines are only meaningful for that field). A profile whose calibration numbers are copied, not measured (laya) says UNCALIBRATED in its _source.

typesafe-jev._source: window: the measured hard input ceiling; questions: the per-call cap every batcher plans under; price: docs.typesafe.ai, checked 2026-09-16

laya._source: Laya (open, Apache-2.0; github convaiinnovations/laya), run locally with laya-serve. window: typed-decisions is selectable by model name and keeps 1024 tokens of input, measured; the server drops the rest and says so (usage.truncated). NO calibration yet: every line below is the Jev line copied so the door runs, UNCALIBRATED until measured on Laya.
